findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide a current CFPM certificate during the inspection. The inspector tried to walk them through finding the copy they said they had online but they could not remember which company they received it from. They also stated that the current people with manager certificates were themselves and one other. A hand out was given during the inspection for the local CFPM courses/tests in the area. Ensure that there is always a CFPM available at the facility at all times that foods or food contact items are being handled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the two sani buckets in the facility were observed low on the inspector’s test strips. The facility made new buckets of sanitizer to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times while in use at the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Acoustic type ceiling tiles are observed in the bathrooms. Ceiling coverings should be smooth and easily cleanable. The locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. 

The kit intended for clean-up of vomit/diarrheal events is missing the chemical needed for disinfection of the affected area. The PIC was consulted and quickly ran to the store in order to acquire bleach for this procedure. They also stated that a new kit will be purchased/ordered for future use. They returned with the bleach during this inspection and was walked through its use in relation to these procedure. Ensure that the procedures needed for these events have all needed supplies available at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to actuate the paper towel dispenser, recontaminating their hands. Food service began directly after this event was observed. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all food handlers properly wash their hands prior to food service, and that the hand washing procedures do not allow for re-contamination of the hands prior to food handling practices.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM was available at the facility on inspector’s arrival. The manager arrived during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that enough CFPMs are on staff so that one is on site at all times of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to grabbing a paper towel. Education was conducted with the PIC. They are instructed to educate employees and ensure proper hand washing techniques are used.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No Certified Food Manager present at time of inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM course to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single service paper cookie sleeves observed stored below the handwashing sink. Store single service/food contact items where they are protected from potential contamination. Relocate so that they are not below the handwashing sink where they may be subject to leaks.
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No Certified Food Manager present at time of inspection. Ensure sufficient staff have completed CFM course to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed picking something up off the floor (from a pile of waste), donning gloves, and handling food without washing hands. Wash hands after any task that may have contaminated hands. CORRECTED-- Discussed handwashing with PIC and employee and provided education.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels present in the womens restroom. CORRECTED-- Paper towels provided.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Meatballs observed to be 104F (probed) in the hot holding unit. Ensure hot held foods are maintained 135F or above. CORRECTED-- Meatballs voluntarily discarded.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Neither of the two employees present have completed food handler training despite having been employed at the facility for more than 30 days. Staff must complete food handler training.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed customer soda fountain nozzles to have an accumulation of slime. CORRECTED- PIC will clean and sanitize soda nozzles. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized as often as necessary to prevent soil build-up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Observed flies throughout the kitchen, mainly in the back kitchen and storage areas.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES. (C)
See 6-202.13 in the 2017 FDA Food Code for information on food-safe pest control methods.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Packages of 3 cookies observed with no labels. Pre packaged foods must have proper labels. 750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed cardboard both be used in the singles service utensil holder on toaster oven. Single service utensils are wrapped but the dividers must be of a clean able nature. 750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily clean able

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Observed single use wrapper for the sandwiches to be in a pile under the hand sink cabinet. A chunk that was on the bottom of the cabinet was removed so that they could be counted and discarded. Properly protect single service items. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed a sanitizer bucket on the front line that was at 100 ppm quat. Manager was notified. All sanitizer buckets should be maintained at a concentration of 200 ppm when using quat and checked with test strips. Employee replaced the sanitizer bucket.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed a clean knife on a magnet strip that was holding up a "to-do list." Manager was notified that this is an improper practice as the paper had been wrote on and handled, then was placed on a clean utensil. Utensil was removed for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in cooler to have an accumulation of a discolored liquid and debris in the back of the cooler. Manager stated the cooler had began leaking recently and was placed in for work order. Manager was also unsure whether something had been spilled from the night before. Ensure floors are kept in good repair, as well as in a clean state. Manager cleaned the floor during inspection.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed multiple employee drinks on a food prep surface with no lid or straw. Drinks should have a straw, lid, and be stored below and away from food. Ensure that employee drinks are handled in the  proper manner. Drinks were discarded during spot check.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510d Observed employees improperly washing their hands. Staff was observed turning off the faucet with clean hands prior to drying hands with clean hands. Avoid turning off the soiled faucet with your clean hands. Unroll paper toweling prior to washing hands. Wash hands, dry them, and then use the towel to turn off the water. To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed the frontline sani-bucket to be at 100ppm Quat in solution. Solution should be at 200ppm Quat. During the inspection, the bucket was emptied and refilled with a proper 200ppm Quat solution. The sani-bucket in the back and the three compartment sink was properly set-up. This frontline bucket is likely used considerably more than any other bucket in store. Make sure that frequently used cloths/buckets are emptied and refilled frequently enough to maintain solution of 200ppm. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

More the coat and fly swatter to storage location away from food and equipment.  Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
Provide a thermometer in this unit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the yellow plastic tray holding the slicer had some dust and soil. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean this piece of equipment.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed that the damp mop was not hung to dry between uses.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
Hang damp mop hanging upright when not in use so as to promote air-drying to prevent molding.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed that the first shelf above the 3 part sink has a small amount of rust where some of the coating has chipped off. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Repair / recoat this shelf so as to be an easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Observed that there is a hose attached to the mop sink faucet that extends to the drain, causing a condition that could lead to back-flow in the case of a clog or overflow in the drain line plumbing.
750-1080 A hose shall not be attached to a faucet unless a backflow prevention device is installed. Install backflow prevention device.
Remove hose from drain area, so as not to cause a condition which could lead to back-flow.
CORRECTED= hose was removed from drain.

findings.comment:
Observed that the wall behind the prep table has some splash and soil.  
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. 
Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: There were no thermometers for the following coolers:  (A) on the front line under the microwave ovens, and (B) drink cooler with the yogurt in the customer area.  Put thermometers in the two units.  750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: The following surfaces were rusty / moldy:   (A) rusty bottom of shelf above the 3-pan sink,   (B) moldy wall-to-sink caulk joint behind the 3-pan sink,    (C) rusty spot on the water heater,     (D) panel coming off the water heater shelf.    Sand and paint all rusty surfaces, remove moldy caulk joint on the 3-pan sink and re-caulk the gap,  re-attach the panel on the water heater shelf.        750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth and washable and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The magnetic knife holder is rusty / soiled.   Clean and sanitize the knife holder or replace it.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
There was no lid on the waste basket in the men's restroom.  Put a lid on the waste basket.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.comment:
The vent in the ceiling near the water heater is soiled.  Clean the vent.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.comment:

.820) Spray bottle of QUAT sanitizing solution also tests at 0 ppm using both test strips.  A new bottle of solution for sanitizing surfaces was mixed and it now tests at 400 ppm QUAT.
